::: {.why}
The combination you computed last night beat every component, and understanding why is the difference between running a trend follower and running a portfolio of trend followers.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the pairwise correlation of the same trend rule across instruments and say what it implies for the combination's Sharpe.
- Say what a trend follower is long, in option terms, and what it pays for that exposure.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Explain the combination gain with numbers: report the correlation matrix of your four trend signals' returns, and check that the observed combination Sharpe matches what the correlations predict. Trend rules on different asset classes are close to uncorrelated, which is the entire reason managed futures exists as a business.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Extend to more instruments and more lookbacks: build the same rule at 1, 3, 6 and 12 month lookbacks across every instrument you have, and report the Sharpe of the full combination against the best single specification. Log every specification. The point is that combining beats selecting, and it does so without requiring you to have chosen correctly.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The trend follower becomes a portfolio of trend rules across instruments and lookbacks, combined rather than selected, with the correlation structure that justifies the combination measured rather than assumed.
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A cross-instrument, cross-lookback trend book with the correlation matrix and the combination Sharpe against the best single specification.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Four trend rules each with a Sharpe of 0.4 combine to 0.8. What correlation does that imply, and did you measure it or assume it?
:::
